findings: The ideation novelty gate is complete for the configured Google Sheet scope only: all 543 pending/accepted rows were compared, with 543 sheet-summary reviews and latest-source inspection of all 14 plausible or unclear rows. The four blank-summary rows (PRs 2207–2210) are included in those latest-source reviews; no read errors, overlap, or unresolved ambiguity remains. Sheet-summary evidence is correctly retained as weaker than original-rubric verification.

The closest catalog tasks remain meaningfully distinct: PR-520 “Cap a cocktail shaker and shake it with both hands without spilling,” PR-740 “Hold a vial up to a counting tray’s chute…,” PR-1156 “Mix the two layers in a separatory funnel,” PR-1436 “Free the ice cubes,” PR-1592 “Pour and sort mixed coins,” PR-2048 “Lift each gnocchi…with a slotted spoon,” and PR-2130 “Empty the sink strainer into the bin.” None tests aperture-mediated separation of an intermixed batch while retaining the larger workpieces in the manipulated screen. All six required benchmark definition sets are pinned and covered by selector/registry-aware comparisons. Closest original tasks are LIBERO “put_the_cream_cheese_in_the_bowl,” RoboCasa “ShakePan” and “DrainVeggies,” SimplerEnv “PutOnInSceneEnv,” BEHAVIOR “clean_a_sieve-0” and “pouring_water_in_a_glass-0,” DataCenterBench “DC-join — Join the Ethernet plug and coupler,” and RoboDojo “pour_balls_into_vase.” RoboDojo supplies substantive many-body pouring overlap, but none of these tasks tests selective physical passage of one intermixed population while retaining another.

The selected objective and essential mechanism are clear: bimanual load sharing, physical agitation of a rigid apertured screen, orientation-dependent passage of eight free ceramic-media bodies, retention of two free steel washers, support reseating, release, and a fresh three-second dwell. Novelty does not rest on color, layout, object naming, or a prescribed motion sequence.

Industrial relevance is source-grounded by Raytech’s manual sifting screens and media-separation guidance: https://www.raytech-ind.com/media/wysiwyg/raytech/RaytechCatalog.pdf, https://raytech-ind.com/manual-separating.html, and https://raytech-ind.com/the-art-and-science-of-mass-finishing.
